Its first activation comes at the end of the Wizard Phase, after all other figures in that phase have activated, unless that's its normal phase, in which case it activates in the normal order. Its second activation comes at the end of the Soldier Phase; again, unless that is its normal phase, in which case it activates in the normal order. The figure still gains the standard number of actions per activation.

rows.name: 998. Life Drain
rows.text: This figure does double damage in melee combat against all living targets, so excluding undead and constructs.

rows.name: 999. Powerful
rows.text: This figure does double damage in melee combat.

rows.name: 1000. Three Lives
rows.text: This figure literally has three lives. Essentially it can roll the "Dead" result on the survival table twice before it actually dies. The first two times, treat the result as "Full Recovery" instead.

rows.name: Creating & running a Vampire
rows.text: Creating a Vampire (GM/NPC villain, or PC by group agreement): same starting stats as a wizard, same item slots minus armour/shields. No apprentices (may nominate a warband member as one per game); 9 soldiers (4 specialist). School "Vampire" — Aligned (+2): Chronomancer, Necromancer, Soothsayer; Neutral (+4): Elementalist, Enchanter, Illusionist, Sigilist, Summoner, Witch; Antithetical: Thaumaturge (never learnable). Starts with 8 spells: 3 Vampire, 1 per aligned school, 2 from 2 neutral schools. Traits: Undead, Immune to Control Undead, Magic Attacks, Mind Lock, Thaumaturgic Vulnerability, True Sight, Partial Immunity to Normal Damage. New levels cost 120xp (max 300xp/game); Will capped at +5; Health cap 22; can't learn/cast Transcendence; can't benefit from Heal/Miraculous Cure/Healing Potions; Animal Companion yields an undead animal; never has Rangifers; regains Health equal to damage dealt to giants in melee. Unnatural Health: no natural post-game healing — pay 5gc per Health point regained, or consume a permanent (non-undead/construct/demon) warband member's blood instead (removes them from the roster, replaceable next game; vampire runs at 8 soldiers that game); failing to pay at 0 Health counts as a Dead result. Sun Damage: 1 damage per activation in uncovered sunlight. Becoming a Vampire (usually accidental): gains all vampire traits/rules, loses Thaumaturge spells (all other Casting Numbers +1), Will capped at +5, level recalculated down for lost/degraded spells and Will, school becomes Vampire, loses apprentice (gains a 9th soldier slot instead). A card-deck version of the 8 Vampire spells ("Vampire Spell Cards") appears in the book's appendix, identical in effect. Running Creature Spellcasters (GM technique, reusable for any monster spellcaster): Recruit Another Player to run it; Fight and Switch (play the scenario twice, swapping sides); Shared Control (control passes between players, e.g. per-turn or by secret bid); or an Instruction List (attack spells vs. visible enemies first, buffs otherwise, and generally move away from warband members rather than toward them to keep casting).

Blood Legacy.title: Fire Giant Wizard (deferred mechanic — reference only)

rows.name: Creating & running a Fire Giant Wizard
rows.text: Fire giants share every school except Chronomancer (purely human), plus unique giant-only grimoires. Creating a Fire Giant Wizard (for very hard/large encounters, not balanced campaign play): M6 F+4 S+0 A14 W+4 H22; no armour/shields; can't learn/use Chronomancer spells or Write Scroll (can still sell such grimoires/scrolls); a found magic weapon is giant-usable only on a 16+ (else sell/vault it); potions are human-sized unless two doses are combined into one giant-sized dose (1 slot); other magic items resize to fit. No apprentices. School "Fire Giant" — Aligned (+2): Enchanter, Elementalist, Soothsayer; Neutral (+4): Illusionist, Necromancer, Sigilist, Summoner, Thaumaturge, Witch; Antithetical: Chronomancer. Traits: Large, Strong, Elemental Resistance (2). Levels cost 200xp (max 400xp/game); Health cap 30; empowering costs 2 Health per +1 (not 1-for-1) due to Elemental Resistance. A card-deck version ("Fire Giant Spell Cards") appears in the appendix.

rows.name: Giant-Blooded
rows.text: Giant-Blooded (generic modification, applicable to any core-rulebook standard/specialist soldier, one per warband, not to animals/demons/constructs/undead): declared at hire, +50gc, gives -1 Move, -2 Will, +2 Health, and the Giant-Blooded trait (+1 melee damage, +4 to TN-based Fight rolls, includes Large). Two convenience tables of pre-built giant-blooded versions of every core soldier type exist in the source, priced at base+50gc.

rows.name: Optional rules
rows.text: Increased Specialists: +1 specialist slot per full 20 levels (0–19: 4, 20–39: 5, 40–59: 6, 60–79: 7, 80+: 8). Increased Item Slots: wizard & apprentice each +1 slot at level 30 and 70 (max +2). Increased Max Health: +1 potential Health cap per full 10 levels, to a max of 30 (0–9: 20 ... 100+: 30); stacks on top of other Health-cap rules like lichdom or vampirism. Lower Casting Minimum: level 100+ wizards may reduce Casting Numbers to a minimum of 4 (from 5). Alternate XP Expenditure (no level effect): 100XP=100gc; 20XP = +1 to one Out-of-Game Casting Roll (max +5/casting); 1XP = 2gc toward potion ingredients; 1XP = 3gc toward a new apprentice; 25XP = one extra Black Market roll usable on any potion/weapon/armour/magic-item/grimoire-spell table from any book (max 100XP/scenario this way).

rows.name: NPC vampire warbands
rows.text: Reusable subsystem for running an NPC (or PC) vampire-led warband in any campaign. Build the vampire per the rules above, leveled to (opposing wizard's level - 5) if that's above level 5. Six henchmen: 3 soldiers of any type/book (under Thralldom, -1 Will) and 3 ghouls (each may get a two-handed weapon, hand weapon+shield, or +1 Move). Vampire activates in the Wizard Phase (3 henchmen, group activation allowed); a chosen second-in-command henchman activates in the Apprentice Phase (3 more); remainder activate in the Soldier Phase. The vampire warband earns no XP and can't interact with treasure tokens.

Blood Legacy.title: Ambush Cards (24-card generic deck)
Blood Legacy.blurb: Before a scenario, each player draws a fixed number of cards (6 for the source campaign; 4 suggested for general use) and plays them secretly whenever their stated trigger condition is met, one per turn max. Full text of all 24:

entries.name: Zombie Troll
entries.text: Start of turn: place a zombie troll in any corner.

entries.name: Spectre
entries.text: Start of turn: place a spectre in any corner.

entries.name: Frost Wraith
entries.text: Start of turn: place a frost wraith in any corner.

entries.name: Blood-drinker Bat
entries.text: End of turn (after creatures act): place one, 3"+ from any warband member.

entries.name: Mist-Walker
entries.text: End of turn (after creatures act): place one, 6"+ from any warband member.

entries.name: Armoured Skeletons
entries.text: End of turn: place 2 at any table-edge midpoint, 3"+ from a warband member.

entries.name: Zombies
entries.text: Start of creature phase: place one in a corner; it activates this phase.

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.text: Start of creature phase: place one at a table-edge midpoint; it activates this phase.

entries.name: Bones of the Earth
entries.text: Start of turn: cast on a chosen warband member at Casting Roll 14.

entries.name: Dispel
entries.text: End of any phase: cancel one active spell.

entries.name: Bone Dart
entries.text: End of any phase: a non-spellcaster warband member suffers a +5 shooting attack.

entries.name: Blink
entries.text: End of any phase: cast Blink on a non-spellcaster at Casting Roll 16.

entries.name: Fool's Gold
entries.text: Start of turn: cast Fool's Gold (Casting Roll 16) on a treasure-carrying figure.

entries.name: Fog
entries.text: Start of any phase: 6"×3"×1" fog line anywhere; lasts 3 turns.

entries.name: Draining Word

Fireheart.title: Construct Modification (deferred mechanic — reference only)
Fireheart.blurb: Animate Construct is Out of Game (B) for a first warband, but usually (A) afterward; each spellcaster may cast it once between games (repair/re-animation below has its own separate limit). A scroll can animate a "standard" small/medium/large construct with no roll, or modify an existing one — but scrolls can never animate-with-modification simultaneously, and never repair/re-animate. Constructs can't drink or receive potions unless a potion explicitly allows it. Repair & Re-Animation via Animate Construct: fixing a permanent injury is -4 to the roll (pre-game); reviving a "dead" construct is -6 (post-game only, by its own wizard) — success revives it, a natural 1 destroys it forever, any other failure leaves it inanimate for another attempt after a later game (no need to be the very next game, unlike Miraculous Cure). Only "standard" (small/medium/large) constructs can ever be modified; bestiary constructs from other books can't be (they're already modified).

rows.name: Construct Modification rules
rows.text: Construct Modification: constructs have no item slots but may take exactly one modification (two under an optional variant, which then always makes it a specialist soldier). The Modification Table below doubles as a Treasure Table; Black Market rules allow trading up to 2 rolls/game for it. New-with-modification costs an extra -2 to Animate Construct (cumulative with size); modifying an existing one costs -2 alone. Every modification (unless marked "No modification penalty") also imposes a permanent -1 to one stat of the owner's choice. Superseded prior items: Construct Crossbow (Maze of Malcor) → Projectile Weapon; Construct Hammer (rulebook/Folio) → the entry below; Construct Oil (Folio) → the entry below; Construct Spikes (Red King) → the entry below; Construct Varnish (Malcor) → Elemental Armour; Golem Flesh (Forgotten Pacts) → Improved Joints.

The Wildwoods.title: Chapter One: Rules of the Wild
The Wildwoods.blurb: Before a wilderness game, roll for Dominant Terrain (d20): 1–4 Forest, 5–8 Mountain, 9–12 Bog, 13–16 Ice, 17–20 Urban — mix in other terrain types regardless for a dense table.

entries.name: Mountain / Precipice

entries.name: Bog

entries.name: Amphibious Creatures

entries.name: Urban

The Wildwoods.title: Supplies & Cargo Transports (deferred mechanic — reference only)

rows.name: Supply Points (sp)
rows.text: Supply Points (sp): buy at 1gc/sp, sell at 2sp/gc. After every wilderness scenario each warband member consumes 2sp (1 consumed = "hungry," -2 Health/-1 Will next game; 0 consumed = "very hungry," -5 Health/-2 Will) — only cured by consuming supplies afterward, not in-game healing. Casting any Out of Game spell costs 1sp. A warband can carry 50sp unaided; starting a wilderness campaign, add 200gc earmarked for a transport + 50sp.

rows.name: Cargo Transport

Adjacent figures may load unlimited treasure onto it for safekeeping/exit. Enemies can melee it (Fight+0, Armour12): winning lets them steal 1 token, loot 5sp (once/figure/game), destroy sp equal to damage, or destroy it outright if it's already empty/would hit 0. Only Large creatures can destroy it outright otherwise. Immune to bow/crossbow/javelin unless Elemental-Hammer'd (then up to 5sp); has no Will (auto-fails Will-based spells): Blink randomly shifts 1", Crumble costs 5sp (or destroys it), Petrify stops it a turn, Push caps at 3", Slow caps it at 1", Telekinesis can move it 1" in LoS. Spellcaster Magazine.title: Horses in Frostgrave (Issue 1 — deferred mechanic, reference only)
Spellcaster Magazine.blurb: A full optional mounted-combat subsystem. Requires the Stable base resource (300gc, keeps one horse, doesn't affect warband limit); a horse then costs 200gc. Only one horse per warband at a time. Any model may ride except Animals, Undead, Demons, and Constructs; models start mounted by default and take a horse as a 1-slot item. Rider+horse count as one Large model for size purposes.

rows.text: Fine.
Rider Thrown: 1 damage, dismounted.
Heavy Landing: 3 damage, dismounted.
Snap: horse injured (removed as casualty, survival roll as a Soldier); rider immediately removed as casualty (normal survival roll).

rows.name: Melee Training
rows.text: 200gc - Gains 'Two Heads' (Forgotten Pacts p.17).

rows.name: Sure-footed
rows.text: 250gc - -2 to Stumble Table rolls.

rows.name: Aggressive
rows.text: 400gc - +1 Fight to Riderless profile and Mounted Modifiers.

rows.name: Loyal
rows.text: 400gc - +3 Will to Riderless profile; can never be rustled.

rows.name: Barding
rows.text: 600gc - +2 Armour, -2 Move to both profiles.

rows.name: Charger
rows.text: 500gc - Gains 'Horns' (Forgotten Pacts p.16).

rows.name: Note 2
rows.text: If the rider is removed as a casualty, the horse activates in the creature phase and moves toward its deployment zone. Every time Rough Ground affects a mounted figure's movement, roll on the Stumble Table (Jumping: same table, +4 to the roll after landing):

rows.name: Note 3
rows.text: A mounted soldier may never climb. Carrying treasure mounted needs 4 actions across activations (dismount, pick up, load, remount) and only one token at a time, with no movement penalty while carried mounted. A warband that captures and keeps an enemy horse must immediately buy a Stable. Control Animal / Mind Control targets the Riderless profile for the Will roll; on a fail, the rider is thrown and the horse is mind-controlled (any treasure stays on the horse).

Spellcaster Magazine.title: Dungeon Hazards (Issue 1 — reusable GM toolkit, reference only)
Spellcaster Magazine.blurb: Three reusable hazard mechanics pulled from the "Catacombs of the Evrenbright" mini-campaign (the campaign's plot and scenarios themselves are scenario-specific and omitted).

entries.name: Confusion Gas
entries.text: A figure exposed to a mind-altering gas rolls d20 on a chart of random moves/attacks; on activating normally it must also pass a Will Roll TN16 or get 0 actions.

entries.name: Phantasmic Sphere
entries.text: Drifting hazardous-terrain disk: indestructible, drifts 4" randomly each creature phase. Anyone touched makes a Will Roll TN10, takes damage equal to the amount failed by, and is pushed 1" away. Blocks LoS; a figure "killed" by one gets +3 to its survival roll.

entries.name: Marker Swap
entries.text: On first contact with a trap-door/spike-trap marker, roll a die: 12+ becomes treasure (plus a random creature within 6"); below 12 becomes a random creature (plus optional treasure within 6").

rows.text: Subject to Critical Hits
No Elemental Damage Resistance
One Eye — -4 Fight defending vs. shooting
Weak-Willed — Will reduced to +2
Allergic — -4 Armour vs. a specific substance
Susceptible to Poison — not immune; breathes fire instead of spitting poison
Fear of Undead — always attacks undead in LoS first

rows.name: Falling onto stairs or slopes
rows.text: Falling onto stairs or slopes: if pushed onto a slope/staircase steeper than 30°, make a Move Roll TN14 — success moves the figure halfway down, failure all the way to the bottom; either way, resolve falling damage as normal, then halve it (round down).

Spellcaster Magazine.title: Rangifer Shaman (Issue 3 — deferred mechanic, reference only)

rows.name: Rangifer cultural traits & the Shaman
rows.text: All rangifer share three cultural traits: Hate Undead (+1 Fight vs. undead, magic attacks, only while armed with antlers/flint/wood), Antlers (never unarmed; -1 Fight if antlers are the only weapon), and Flint Weapons (destroyed on any natural 1 rolled in combat).

rows.name: Shaman leveling
rows.text: Rangifer Shaman — a distinct spellcaster restricted to the Rangifer Spell List. Starting line M7 F+2 Sh+0 A12 W+3 H12; 4 starting spells, 5 item slots, free starting weapon; may hire a "hide" of up to 5 rangifer for 200gc. Every 100 XP = 1 level; per level improve a stat (Fight max +5, Shoot max +5, Will max +8, Health max 18), lower a known spell's casting number by 1 (min 5), or learn a new spell (no grimoire needed).

rows.name: Book of the Rangifer
rows.text: A wizard with a Book of the Rangifer (Thaw of the Lich Lord p.47) may hire any one of these (except the Boar) as their one rangifer, at listed cost +80gc; a War-Leader takes the captain's place.

Spellcaster Magazine.title: Underworld Favours: A Debt Economy (Issue 3 — deferred mechanic, reference only)

rows.name: Loan
rows.text: Cost 1 Marker / 100gc (min 100, max 1,000) · Effect Gold added immediately.

rows.name: Intimidation
rows.text: Cost 1 Marker (+1 more per +1 modifier, max 3) · Effect Opposed d20 (intimidator's modifiers vs. target's Will); win = target misses next game; lose = lose half Markers spent (round up).

rows.name: Muscle
rows.text: Cost Per Hired Muscle Table · Effect Up to 2 hired muscle/game, don't count against warband size; +1 Marker if hired muscle dies.
Pay off as many Markers as possible from Treasury gold (150gc each); if none can be paid, treat as 7–12.
Sell magic items to pay off at least 1 Marker; if impossible, treat as 13–18.
Warband members (not the wizard) miss the next game; remove 1 Marker per full 50gc of their combined base cost.
Wizard (1–5) or apprentice (6–20) is beaten and receives a permanent injury, on top of any suffered in-game.

rows.name: Note 1
rows.text: Before a game, a wizard may claim one Underworld Favour immediately, for free, adding Underworld Markers to the vault instead of paying up front. Maximum Markers held = wizard Level.

rows.name: Note 2
rows.text: Hired Muscle costs (1 Marker unless noted): Thug, Thief, Trap Expert — 1 Marker each; Assassin, Barber-Surgeon, Burglar (climbs at full speed) — 2 Markers each. Paying off a Marker costs 150gc at any time. After every game with any Markers held, roll a die: rolling ≤ Markers held calls in the debt (roll on the table below).

Spellcaster Magazine.title: Monster Hunting: For Fun and Profit (Issue 5 — deferred mechanic, not transcribed)
Spellcaster Magazine.blurb: Assigns XP values and harvestable components/bounties to every published Frostgrave monster, replacing the flat +5 XP from Experience Table II (Maze of Malcor) but not scenario-specific rewards. Harvesting: the killer claims the listed item free (if not In Combat), or any later figure may claim it via contact + action; claimed items never take a slot. gc-value items sell for that amount; +1 items are spell/potion components — max one dose per kill, usable for +1 to a matching Casting Roll (or 25gc off a Brew Potion component cost). Every spellcaster has a 3-component pouch free; a Spell Component Bag (5gc, 1 slot) holds 10 more. Only one component may be used per roll.

rows.name: Errata (Issue 7)
rows.text: * Errata (Issue 7, Second Edition): Monstrous Form no longer exists in Second Edition — the Chilopendra Horn's effect changes to +10gc instead. † Rangifer's 0 XP is intentional (killing one is a detriment, not a reward). Source codes: FRB=Rulebook, TLL=Thaw of the Lich Lord, IBP=Into the Breeding Pits, FP=Forgotten Pacts, FF=The Frostgrave Folio, MM=Maze of Malcor, PD=Perilous Dark.

Spellcaster Magazine.title: The Maze of Malcor Outtakes (Issue 7)
Spellcaster Magazine.blurb: Weird Event Cards — a generic sub-system for any Maze of Malcor campaign/scenario with more than 2 players. After each game, players vote on who had the worst game; that player draws one random card, kept for future use. A held card may be played in any future Malcor scenario, one per scenario, never before the end of the first turn.

rows.name: Breeding Cages

rows.name: Alchemical Workshop
rows.text: Price 400gc · Effect Once per post-game, mix 2 potions (both consumed): both odd = wasted; both even = take the lower result on the Greater Potion Table (Frostgrave Folio p.45), add to vault; equal but <20 = workshop destroyed, -2 Health next game; one odd/one even = no result, potions recovered.

Spellcaster Magazine.title: The Great Wyrm — AI & the Reveal incantation (Issue 7)
Spellcaster Magazine.blurb: A fully reusable Old-Dragon-class creature (per Issue 2's dragon categories), usable in any Frostgrave game with its own AI priority list for unplayed use.

rows.name: AI priority (unplayed)
rows.text: AI priority (unplayed): (1) breathe on the nearest treasure-carrier in LoS (or closest figure); (2) Spelleater the most recent spell on itself; (3) True Sight if any figure is invisible; (4) Steal Health on the nearest warband member; (5) Banish any demon in LoS; (6) otherwise move toward the closest warband member in LoS, never straying more than 6" from a treasure pile.

rows.name: Reveal incantation
rows.text: Generic casting variant introduced alongside it: a wizard/apprentice may cast a "Reveal" incantation (CN12, empowerable) as an action that can replace the move; it doesn't count as "casting a spell" for the turn.

entries.name: Legendary Soldiers (Issue 4)

entries.name: Monster Hunting (Issue 5)
